questions: Does 'subsequence' mean a sequence derived by deleting some (or no) elements without changing the order of the remaining elements, as is standard?

Is the subsequence required to be strictly increasing in value, or strictly increasing in index? The phrase 'strictly increasing' typically refers to the values, but the subsequence is of elements, so it's ambiguous whether indices must also increase (they must by definition of subsequence).

For the condition 'consists only of elements at most X_i', does it apply to each element's value individually (A_j ≤ X_i) or to the entire subsequence's maximum? The wording 'elements at most X_i' suggests each element individually.

The guarantee says X_i ≥ min{A_1,...,A_R_i}. Does this imply there is always at least one element ≤ X_i in the prefix, but could all elements be > X_i? No, because min ≤ X_i ensures at least one element ≤ X_i.

When selecting a subsequence from (A_1,...,A_R_i), must the indices be within 1..R_i, or can we only consider elements with indices ≤ R_i? The notation (A_1,...,A_R_i) clearly indicates prefix up to index R_i.

Is the subsequence allowed to be empty? If yes, the maximum length could be 0 if no element ≤ X_i, but the guarantee ensures at least one such element, so empty case might not occur. However, if all elements > X_i despite guarantee? Guarantee prevents that.

For the subsequence, must the elements be distinct in value because it's strictly increasing? Strictly increasing implies distinct values, but could the same value appear at different indices? Since strictly increasing means A_j < A_k for j<k, same value cannot appear.

Does 'maximum possible length' mean over all subsequences satisfying the conditions, we want the length of the longest such subsequence? The clarification says only length required, not tie-breaking, confirming that.
